title: Les adjectifs : place et accord
ruleNote: Most French adjectives come AFTER the noun and agree in gender — 'un chat noir' (m), 'une maison verte' (f, add -e). A few common ones — petit, grand, joli, beau — come BEFORE the noun: 'un petit chien'.

exercises.prompt: Construis : « He has a black cat. »
exercises.explanation: Color adjectives follow the noun: 'chat noir'. 'chat' is masculine → noir.
exercises.hint: Color goes after the noun; chat is masculine → noir.

exercises.prompt: Construis : « She has a small dog. »
exercises.explanation: 'petit' comes BEFORE the noun. 'chien' is masculine → petit.
exercises.hint: petit goes before the noun; chien is masculine → petit.

exercises.prompt: Choisis l'adjectif : une ___ maison (a big house)
Choisis l'adjectif : un chat ___ (a happy cat)
exercises.explanation: 'chat' is masculine singular → content (no ending added).

exercises.prompt: Construis : « The big dog eats an apple. »
exercises.translation: The big dog eats an apple.

exercises.prompt: Construis : « She likes the green house. »
exercises.explanation: Color follows the noun. 'maison' is feminine → verte (add -e).
exercises.hint: Color after the noun; maison is feminine → verte.
